physicalNotes: Radius 2.37 +/- 0.22 Earth radii from Sarkis et al. (2018, AJ 155, 257; arXiv:1805.00830, Table 2), at 6378.137 km per Earth radius. No gravitational parameter is adopted. A sphere: no oblateness is measured.

sources.shape: Inclination 89.5785 degrees from Sarkis et al. (2018), Table 2. The scaled distance a/R* = 74.78 is DERIVED here, not quoted: Kepler's third law with their period, their stellar mass 0.359 solar masses and their stellar radius 0.411 solar radii.
sources.phase: Sarkis et al. (2018), Tables 2 and 3: T0 = BJD 2457264.39144, the time of inferior conjunction, here BMJD 57263.89144.
sources.orientation: Display convention: transit photometry does not measure the orbit's position angle on the sky, so the ascending node is set at position angle 0 (celestial north).
sources.eccentricity: Sarkis et al. (2018), Table 3 (joint HARPS and CARMENES-VIS radial velocities): e = 0.20 +/- 0.08.
sources.argumentOfPeriapsis: Sarkis et al. (2018), Table 3: omega = -0.10 (+0.81/-0.59) rad, fitted with RadVel, whose transit convention f = pi/2 - omega is the one this record uses; here 354.27 degrees.
